points: The Q3 2026 print will reveal whether Azure growth is holding near the ~43% rate reports suggest for the prior quarter or starting to decelerate; sustained momentum is the main driver of the long case.
Cloud gross margin and operating leverage will show if heavy AI capex is being absorbed or still pressuring profitability; margin stability supports the path to FY2 EPS of $23.57.
Management's guidance for Q4 and FY2027 capex will reveal whether the AI build-out is entering a digestion phase or still ramping; a flattening or disciplined spend trajectory supports the long.
Commercial cloud bookings and AI monetization, including Copilot and Azure OpenAI consumption, will show if the 14.3% FY1 EPS growth is backed by revenue conversion or still mostly investment.
The 20-up/9-down analyst revision skew and +2% 90-day revenue drift already lean long; the print needs to confirm that optimism is justified by demand and margin execution.
Valuation is fair versus the theme at 0.9x P/E and 1.0x PEG, so the long depends on execution rather than multiple expansion; the print must show earnings can grow into the FY2 consensus.
watch: Azure revenue growth rate: holding near or above the prior quarter's reported ~43% supports the long; a material slowdown undercuts it.
Cloud gross margin: stable or expanding supports the long; contraction undercuts the FY2 EPS path.
FY2027 capex guidance: a flattening or slower ramp supports the long; another large step-up without matching revenue visibility undercuts it.
Commercial cloud bookings / AI contribution: sustained double-digit growth supports the long; weak conversion undercuts it.
